description: Return the integer arithmetic derivative D(n) over a bounded nonnegative domain.

output.encoding: D(n), where D(0)=D(1)=0, D(p)=1 for primes, and D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)

contract.definition: For n=product(p^e), D(n)=n*sum(e/p) over distinct prime factors p; D(0)=D(1)=0
contract.primary_method: Trial-factor n and add (original_n/p)*e for each distinct prime p with exponent e
contract.independent_method: Recursively choose the least prime divisor p, write n=p*q, and evaluate D(n)=p*D(q)+q from D(1)=0
contract.invalid_cases: Null input, empty/non-exact frame, trailing word, negative n, or n>10^12 returns -1
contract.distinction: This is the integer derivation satisfying the Leibniz product rule; it is not the Möbius, Liouville, totient, divisor-count, or factorization-output function

complexity.primary_time: O(sqrt(n)) trial divisions, at most 500,000 candidate divisors through sqrt(n) for n<=10^12, plus at most 39 factor-removal iterations
complexity.independent_time: At most 39 recursive product-rule steps, each finding a least prime divisor using at most 500,000 trial candidates; at most 19,500,000 candidates total
complexity.independent_space: O(log(n)) recursion depth, at most 39 product-rule steps and 40 stack frames including the base call
